{{Biathlon World Championships 2016}}
'''The 48th [[Biathlon World Championships]]''' was held in [[Oslo]], [[Norway]] from 3 to 13 March 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.biathlonworld.com/en/press_releases.html/do/detail?presse=1663|title=Oslo and Hochfilzen Selected as World Championship Host|date=September 2, 2012|publisher=biathlonworld.com|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120904224920/http://www.biathlonworld.com/en/press_releases.html/do/detail?presse=1663|archive-date=September 4, 2012}}</ref>

There were 11 competitions in total: sprint, pursuit, individual, mass start, relay races for men and women, and mixed relay. All the events during this championships also counted towards the Biathlon World Cup.

==Host selection==
Oslo was the sole candidate for this championship. Oslo was announced as the host city on 2 September 2012 during the X [[International Biathlon Union|IBU]] Congress in [[Merano]], [[Italy]]. Two years earlier Oslo lost [[Biathlon World Championships 2015]] to Kontiolahti.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.biathlonworld.com/en/press_releases.html/do/detail?presse=1029|title=IBU World Championships 2015 to be held in Kontiolahti|publisher=Biathlonworld.com|access-date=February 26, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203025435/http://www4.biathlonworld.com/en/press_releases.html/do/detail?presse=1029|archive-date=December 3, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> This was the sixth time that these World Championships were held in Oslo; the city had previously hosted the event in [[Biathlon World Championships 1986|1986]], [[Biathlon World Championships 1990|1990]] (certain events held in Oslo due to difficult weather in the host city of Minsk), [[Biathlon World Championships 1999|1999]] (certain events held in Oslo due to difficult weather in the host city of Kontiolahti), [[Biathlon World Championships 2000|2000]] and [[Biathlon World Championships 2002|2002]] (only the mass start as it was not on the program for the 2002 Olympics).
